339310093.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Sickle-shaped peritoneal reflection attached to the anterior and superior (diaphragmatic) surfaces of the liver and to the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm, separating the anatomical right and left lobes.
339310093.keyConcept: The falciform ligament connects the liver to the anterior abdominal wall; its free inferior margin contains the ligamentum teres hepatis (obliterated left umbilical vein) and small paraumbilical veins.

1276523692.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Green pear-shaped hollow sac situated on the visceral surface of the liver in the gallbladder fossa, with its fundus projecting beyond the sharp inferior border.
1276523692.keyConcept: The fundus of the gallbladder typically projects beyond the inferior border of the liver at the transpyloric plane, where the lateral border of the rectus abdominis intersects the 9th right costal cartilage.

827391027.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, dominant anatomical lobe lying to the right of the falciform ligament on the diaphragmatic surface, contributing roughly five-sixths of the total hepatic volume.
827391027.keyConcept: Anatomically, the right lobe of the liver is demarcated anteriorly by the falciform ligament, but functionally (Couinaud segmentation), the true functional right liver begins to the right of Cantlie's line.

249727760.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Flattened, wedge-shaped anatomical lobe lying to the left of the falciform ligament on the anterior/diaphragmatic surface of the liver.
249727760.keyConcept: The anatomical left lobe lies to the left of the falciform ligament and fissure for ligamentum venosum, corresponding to Couinaud segments II and III.

1673112297.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Deep transverse fissure on the visceral surface of the liver, bounded anteriorly by the quadrate lobe and posteriorly by the caudate lobe, transmitting the portal triad structures.
1673112297.keyConcept: The porta hepatis serves as the hilum of the liver, transmitting the hepatic portal vein (posteriorly), hepatic artery proper (anterior-left), and bile ducts (anterior-right), enveloped in Glisson's capsule.

899429237.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Centrally located transverse hepatic hilum fissure between the caudate process/lobe above and quadrate lobe below, conveying the portal vein, hepatic artery branches, and hepatic bile ducts.
899429237.keyConcept: The porta hepatis forms the horizontal crossbar of the 'H-shaped' visceral surface of the liver and transmits the components of the portal triad within the free margin of the lesser omentum.

1623608832.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Anterior-inferior longitudinal groove situated on the visceral surface between the left anatomical lobe and the quadrate lobe, housing the obliterated umbilical vein.
1623608832.keyConcept: The fissure for ligamentum teres forms the anterior part of the left longitudinal limb of the hepatic 'H' groove, extending from the inferior border of the liver to the left end of the porta hepatis.

2141877380.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Distinct, rectangular lobe situated on the posterosuperior visceral surface between the fissure for ligamentum venosum (left) and groove for IVC (right), superior to the porta hepatis.
2141877380.keyConcept: The caudate lobe (Spigelian lobe / Couinaud segment I) receives vascular branches from both right and left portal triads and drains directly into the IVC via small independent hepatic veins.

936490482.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Four-sided (rectangular) lobe on the inferior visceral surface, bounded by the fossa for gallbladder on the right, fissure for ligamentum teres on the left, and porta hepatis posteriorly.
936490482.keyConcept: Though anatomically part of the right lobe of the liver, the quadrate lobe functionally belongs to the left liver (Couinaud segment IV) because it receives blood supply from the left hepatic artery and left branch of the portal vein.

2131196612.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Vertical sulcus situated on the posterior surface between the caudate lobe and bare area of the right lobe, accommodating the inferior vena cava.
2131196612.keyConcept: The groove for the IVC forms the posterior part of the right longitudinal limb of the visceral 'H'; hepatic veins emerge here directly to empty into the inferior vena cava.

2064718414.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large non-peritoneal triangular area on the posterior/diaphragmatic surface of the right lobe of the liver, bounded by the superior and inferior layers of the coronary ligament.
2064718414.keyConcept: The bare area of the liver is in direct contact with the diaphragm without intervening peritoneum; its lymphatic vessels drain directly through the diaphragm into posterior mediastinal lymph nodes.

1895515648.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Narrow, deep vertical cleft on the postero-inferior surface separating the caudate lobe from the left anatomical lobe, containing the fibrous remnant of the ductus venosus.
1895515648.keyConcept: The fissure for ligamentum venosum forms the posterior part of the left longitudinal limb of the hepatic 'H' and provides attachment for the two layers of the lesser omentum.

1944659143.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large blue venous vessel occupying the deep vertical groove on the posterior surface of the liver to the right of the caudate lobe.
1944659143.keyConcept: The inferior vena cava (IVC) receives the major hepatic veins directly before piercing the central tendon of the diaphragm at the level of the T8 vertebra.

1964624322.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Four-sided, rectangular lobe on the visceral surface situated between the gallbladder fossa laterally and fissure for ligamentum teres medially, anterior to the porta hepatis.
1964624322.keyConcept: The quadrate lobe is related infero-posteriorly to the pylorus of the stomach and the first part of the duodenum; functionally, it constitutes Couinaud segment IV.

818437915.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent lobe on the posterior surface of the liver, situated between the groove for the IVC on the right, fissure for ligamentum venosum on the left, and porta hepatis inferiorly.
818437915.keyConcept: The caudate lobe features two small processes: the papillary process extending to the left, and the caudate process connecting it to the right lobe between the IVC and porta hepatis (forming the superior boundary of the epiploic foramen of Winslow).

1196110618.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fibrous round cord running in the free inferior edge of the falciform ligament and along the fissure for ligamentum teres on the visceral surface.
1196110618.keyConcept: The ligamentum teres hepatis is the obliterated remnant of the left umbilical vein, which carried oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus.

1562461919.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slender fibrous cord lying within the deep vertical fissure between the caudate lobe and the anatomical left lobe, extending toward the IVC.
1562461919.keyConcept: The ligamentum venosum is the fibrous remnant of the fetal ductus venosus, which shunted oxygenated umbilical vein blood directly to the IVC, bypassing the hepatic sinusoids.

449969610.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Greenish pyriform reservoir attached to the visceral surface of the anatomical right lobe of the liver, comprising a fundus, body, infundibulum, and neck.
449969610.keyConcept: The gallbladder concentrates and stores hepatic bile; its neck narrows into the cystic duct, which contains the spiral fold (spiral valve of Heister) and joins the common hepatic duct to form the bile duct.

434402561.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Smooth, convex, dome-shaped surface of the liver conforming to the concavity of the diaphragm, divided into anterior, superior, and posterior parts and split by the falciform ligament.
434402561.keyConcept: The diaphragmatic surface of the liver is separated from the visceral surface anteriorly by the sharp inferior border; it is covered by visceral peritoneum except at the bare area posteriorly.

1575649729.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Postero-inferior surface of the liver displaying visceral organ impressions, the H-shaped fissures, porta hepatis, gallbladder fossa, and caudate and quadrate lobes.
1575649729.keyConcept: The visceral surface is directed postero-inferiorly and to the left, bearing impressions from abdominal organs including the stomach, duodenum, right kidney, right suprarenal gland, and right colic flexure.
